01
A personal plan

Introduction

Before we begin, we would like to thank you for welcoming us despite our late arrival. The visit allowed us to get to know Lani and Kenzo better, observe some of their behavior and understand the difficulties you are experiencing at home.

Although the main reason for the consultation was inappropriate urination, we also identified other areas that would benefit from training. These include frequent barking, boundaries at home, the relationship between the two dogs, walks and their ability to respond when called.

After assessing the situation, we believe there are two training options that are particularly well suited to your needs. We explain what each one includes and why we recommend them later in this plan.

✦ ✦ ✦
02
Building reliable habits

Toilet Habits and Behavior at Home

Difficulties with toileting

One of your main concerns is that Lani and Kenzo continue to urinate inside the house, including in places where they should not. As you explained, defecation is less of a difficulty, but urination has become a frequent problem.

In Lani's case, you mentioned that this behavior became much more noticeable after she had her puppies. Previously, she seemed to understand better where to relieve herself, but since giving birth she has started urinating in different places.

Motherhood brings physical and hormonal changes, as well as changes in routine. Female dogs also develop natural behaviors associated with keeping their puppies clean, such as stimulating them and removing their waste. These changes, together with the current conditions at home, may be influencing Lani's toilet habits. However, we cannot say that motherhood is the only cause.

Because this change occurred after giving birth, we also recommend asking a veterinarian to rule out urinary problems, especially if Lani has involuntary urine leakage, discomfort or increased urination. Training alone would not resolve an underlying medical cause.

Pad placement and toilet areas

During the visit, we noticed that the dogs have relatively few absorbent pads, usually one or two in their designated toilet areas. We believe this may be making the process more difficult, especially because both dogs spend much of their time indoors.

You also mentioned that they tend to avoid defecating where they have already urinated. If this preference persists, small or already-used surfaces may further limit the places they consider suitable.

We therefore discussed expanding the toilet areas by placing several pads together, possibly four to eight depending on the available space. We also suggested substantially increasing coverage in the enclosed area where Lani stays with her puppies, while always keeping a clean, dry and separate resting area for the mother and puppies.

Dogs generally prefer some separation between their resting, feeding and toilet areas. The layout of these spaces is therefore something we will consider during training.

We also noticed several rugs inside the house. These surfaces can be confusing for dogs accustomed to using pads, particularly when they have not yet learned to clearly distinguish the permitted areas. One of our goals will be to teach them to respect these areas and stop using them as toilet spots.

You told us that you had previously followed our cleaning recommendations, using baking soda, water, vinegar separately and other measures to control odors. Although these initially seemed to help, they are no longer producing the same results.

This reinforces the importance of working directly on the dogs' habits alongside appropriate cleaning.

Routines and schedules

The dogs currently go outside two or three times a day, including a morning outing at around 6:30. They are also fed approximately two or three times a day.

You shared a particularly useful observation: both dogs usually relieve themselves shortly after their morning meal. This pattern helps identify when they need a toilet opportunity and makes it easier to establish predictable habits.

Kenzo presents an additional difficulty, as he does not readily relieve himself outdoors.

The yard consists mainly of concrete blocks with very little soil, while both dogs are accustomed to spending much of the day indoors. This combination of surfaces, habits and toilet opportunities may be contributing to the problem.

During training, we will help both dogs understand which places are appropriate for toileting. We will also assess how to make better use of outings and the time they spend outdoors, respecting their welfare and the family's preferences.

This process requires consistency. Long-established habits generally need repetition and continuity to change in a lasting way.

✦ ✦ ✦
03
A calmer home

Boundaries and Living Together

Furniture and resting places

Another goal you mentioned is preventing the dogs from climbing onto furniture without permission.

You currently use fabrics or covers to protect the furniture, but would like to remove them without constantly worrying about where Lani and Kenzo climb.

A similar situation occurs at night. Although both dogs have their own beds in the bedroom, they often end up sleeping on their owner's bed.

We can address these habits by teaching them to recognize and respect specific boundaries. The aim is for them to continue enjoying family life without requiring constant supervision or instructions for every situation.

It will be important to maintain realistic expectations, as these are behaviors they have practiced for quite some time, and changing them will require consistency.

Frequent barking and attention-seeking

During our visit, we also observed that both dogs bark frequently.

Barking can arise for different reasons, including excitement, insecurity, frustration, alerting or seeking attention. Before trying to reduce it, we need to understand what triggers it and what each dog gains from the behavior.

In Lani's case, you told us that she often interrupts when Kenzo receives attention. When someone starts petting him, she frequently approaches and tries to get petted too.

Although this is often described as jealousy, it may also relate to attention-seeking behavior that has been reinforced over time.

We want to help both dogs share space and their owners' attention more calmly, without feeling the need to constantly interrupt each other.

Feeding and respect for personal space

Another behavior that caught our attention is Lani's tendency to take Kenzo's food.

During the visit, we observed Kenzo trying to retreat to a corner to eat a treat quietly. This may suggest that he is looking for a place to eat without Lani interfering.

Each dog needs to feel safe while eating and resting. When one constantly interrupts the other, tensions or habits can develop that affect their relationship.

We will work to improve this dynamic and help both dogs respect each other's space, food and individual attention time.

A calmer home begins with clearer communication.

04
Confidence beyond home

Walks, Obedience and Socialization

Safety on walks

The dogs currently take short walks around the home. We understand why you avoid certain parts of the neighborhood, especially where stray dogs could pose a risk to two small dogs.

However, walks also play an important role in a dog's life. They provide opportunities to explore, experience different environments, receive stimulation and develop confidence in everyday situations.

One particularly important concern is that Lani and Kenzo do not yet respond reliably when called.

This creates a safety limitation, especially if they accidentally leave the property or find themselves in an open space.

For this reason, recall is one of the obedience goals we recommend addressing, within the scope of the selected program.

Living alongside the Rottweiler

You also explained that you have an elderly female Rottweiler who lives in the yard and has almost no contact with Lani and Kenzo.

We understand the concern about their difference in size, especially because the Rottweiler is older and the Poodles are small.

However, keeping them permanently separated does not eliminate the possibility of an accidental encounter.

We therefore believe it would be beneficial to assess the relationship between all three dogs and gradually work on familiarization. The aim is to help them recognize and respect each other's signals and space, reducing the risk of conflict.

This process must also respect the Rottweiler's age, physical condition and tolerance. We do not aim to force them to live together constantly, but to develop a safer, more manageable relationship.

Specific work involving all three dogs will need to be agreed within the scope of training.

✦ ✦ ✦
05
Wellbeing comes first

Additional Considerations

Lani's motherhood

Lani had her first litter at a very young age, approximately ten or eleven months old, following an accidental mating during heat.

As you explained, the puppies already have families waiting for them, although they are staying with their mother until they reach the appropriate age for separation.

Because Lani is so young, particular attention should be paid to her physical and nutritional recovery. We also discussed the advisability of waiting at least one year and several heat cycles before considering another litter. Any future breeding should depend on a veterinarian confirming that Lani has finished developing and is in suitable condition.

Food quality and stool consistency

The dogs' current food could be of better quality. Improving their diet may help produce firmer stools that are easier to manage and clean up. We recommend Taste of the Wild based on our positive experience with the brand.

Kenzo's medical history

You informed us that Kenzo has had an allergic reaction to NexGard.

This history does not necessarily limit his training, but it must be taken into account when considering any antiparasitic treatment. A veterinarian should determine which products can be used safely.

Pool safety

The property has a swimming pool and, according to what you told us, neither Poodle knows how to swim.

This is a risk that deserves attention, as a dog can accidentally fall into the water while playing, running or moving near the edge.

We believe both dogs would benefit from supervised familiarization with water and learning to find a safe exit. We can assess this through supervised pool or beach sessions as an additional service, subject to availability.

In the meantime, the pool must be protected against accidental access by the dogs. Swimming training does not replace safety barriers or supervision.

Option 1: Simple Basic Obedience (Phase 1)

The economical option

  • Format: Private training.
  • Duration: 5 to 7 sessions.
  • Session length: 45 to 90 minutes.
  • Base package price: ƒ 695.-

This program focuses on improving communication between owners and their dogs, establishing boundaries and developing better control of impulses and everyday behavior.

For Lani and Kenzo, we recommend focusing mainly on living together at home, toilet habits, barking, respect for furniture and resting spaces, attention-seeking and behavior during walks.

It would also help establish a more consistent structure for the two dogs' daily life together.

Its main advantage is that we can focus on the problems currently affecting the family most, without committing to a more extensive program from the outset.

Limitations: This program does not include all formal command training from phase 2 or the outdoor exposure work of phase 3. If you would like dedicated recall sessions, further work on particular behaviors or additional work with the Rottweiler, we can assess extra sessions and agree on their cost.

This is the option we recommend if your priority is mainly to improve behavior at home while keeping the investment lower.

The more comprehensive option

This program integrates the content of the previous phases and adds practical work in different environments and everyday situations.

It is designed for families who want their dogs to behave appropriately both at home and during walks, outings and activities outside their familiar surroundings.

What Both Deep Basic Obedience Options Include

The main difference from the first option is that, in addition to behavior and obedience, this program develops skills in real-life situations.

The dogs can be exposed in a controlled way to places such as Punda, beaches, areas with other animals and our training center, according to what is appropriate for their needs.

This would be especially beneficial for Lani and Kenzo because they currently have limited experience walking in different places and still need to develop a more reliable recall.

It would also help them gain experience and confidence around stimuli they do not usually encounter at home.

Controlled exposure and socialization do not simply mean approaching every dog or person they encounter. Each experience must be adapted to their temperament and behavior so they can learn without becoming overwhelmed.

Main advantage: This is the program we recommend if you want a more comprehensive education that goes beyond resolving household difficulties and allows you to enjoy more activities with your dogs outside the home.

Limitations: It requires a greater investment and commitment to maintaining what they learn. Swimming and dedicated sessions with the Rottweiler should not be considered automatically included; these would be agreed according to the chosen scope.

Lani's board-and-train stay would also need to be scheduled around nursing, weaning and her physical recovery.

08
Finding the right fit

Why Complete Basic Obedience Is Not Our First Recommendation

Complete Basic Obedience remains a good alternative. However, following the assessment, we consider it to sit between the two approaches that may be more suitable for you.

This package combines the behavioral education of phase 1 with the command training of phase 2. However, it does not include the same outdoor exposure and adaptation work as the deep program.

If your priority is resolving problems at home, starting with Simple Basic Obedience may be more economical and appropriate, adding specific sessions only when needed.

If, on the other hand, you would like more comprehensive obedience work, better behavior in different places and greater confidence to help reduce insecurity and constant barking while improving responsiveness outside the home, it makes more sense to invest directly in Deep Basic Obedience.

This allows you to choose a program according to the results you want to achieve, rather than selecting an intermediate option that may not fit your priorities as closely.

How the Recommended Training Would Progress

1. Begin with basic commands

In the first sessions, we would begin with basic commands such as coming when called and sitting.

2. Establish boundaries

Next, we would begin establishing the household boundaries, including rules around furniture and other areas or items that should be off-limits.

3. Continue with the remaining commands

We would then continue teaching the remaining commands in the program.

4. Practice in different places and situations

Throughout the remaining sessions, we would practice what the dogs have learned in different places and situations, helping the owners understand how to guide and manage them.
